name: Find SEO Tools

sources.title: Homepage — 'The place to find SEO tools', 240+ tools across categories; '+ Submit Tool' links to /submit
Submit a tool — Webflow-style form for new tools or updates to already-published tools

requirements: Tool must be relevant to SEOs / digital marketers (categories: Technical SEO, Content, Backlinks, Monitoring & Reporting, Keyword, Tool Suites, platform-specific SEO, training courses)
No pricing or fee is mentioned on the submit form — submission is free
Submissions are reviewed for category fit ('Your tool will be reviewed to see if it fits into other categories')
Non-SEO products would not fit the directory's scope
preparation: Tool name and a ≤9-word value description
Best-fit category plus pricing model: Paid / Free / Free Options (Free Options = permanently free tier, not a trial)
One-or-two-paragraph description starting with the tool name
Website URL, Twitter/X account, launch year
Image URL representing the tool (1280×800 or 8:5); a site screenshot is used as fallback
Submitter name + email; note whether you are the founder/creator
workflow: Fill tool name, ≤9-word pitch, category, pricing model, website, description, Twitter, launch year, image URL
Add submitter details and submit — success shows 'Thank you! Your submission has been received!'
Fallback if the form fails: email submit@findseotools.com
watchFor: The ≤9-word tagline is a hard format constraint — draft it first
'Free Options' specifically means a permanent free tier; don't misclassify a free trial
Founder/creators get an extra opt-in ('we'd love to hear a little about you') — likely used for editorial depth
Form is an embedded Webflow/Airtable-style embed; errors surface inline only
countsAsLive: The tool appears as a card on https://findseotools.com/all-tools or under its category page with website link, pricing badge, and key features
unknowns: Whether listings include a followed outbound link
